Point particles cram all of their interaction into a definite point. When the force involved in an interaction is the gravitational force—that is, when the messenger particle involved in the interaction is the graviton instead of the photon—this complete packing of the force’s punch into a single point leads to disastrous results, such as the infinite answers we alluded to earlier. Strings, by contrast, “smear” out the place where interactions occur. Because different observers perceive that the interaction takes place at various locations along the left part of the surface of Figure 6. 10, in a real sense this means that the interaction location is smcared out among all of them.
